title: Finding the Words – The craft of writing
imageAlt: Black and white photo of a journalist interviewing an artist at a gallery opening, with notebooks, a camera and a laptop on the table; violet notes sketch written genres, the live event, an article structure and the final outcome: a recorded interview and a finished article
summary: A craft workshop for anyone who writes, about culture or for work. You’ll learn how written genres differ, how an article is built and how to run a good interview, then put it into practice by covering a real exhibition or event together.
forWho: Aspiring journalists, communicators and anyone who writes for work, whatever the subject.
levelNote: Open to everyone. You don’t need to care about film to get a lot out of it.

explore.title: Written genres
explore.text: How publications differ, and what makes a profile, a story and a review.

explore.title: How an article is built
explore.text: Structure, breaking a piece into parts, finding its axis or starting point, and the possibilities of creative writing.

explore.title: The interview
explore.text: Preparation, conducting the conversation, the role of detail and environment, building rapport and the psychology of the encounter. Task: record an interview.

explore.title: Covering a live event
explore.text: The group goes to an exhibition or event, interviews the curator or author, gathers material and builds an article together, with the tutor working alongside.

outcome: You’ll leave with a recorded interview and a finished article built from a real cultural event.
